name: build-status-table
description: How STATUS.md is kept: one heading and one table with five fixed columns, one plain statement per cell, a closed status vocabulary, no dependency language, and a checker that rejects anything else. Load it before editing STATUS.md, when adding a work item or changing its status, when a status cell starts to explain instead of state, when someone asks where are we or what is left, and when a report is about to grow prose, sub-bullets, or run-on sentences. Also load it when a row is marked Done without a result, or when a new column seems necessary.

purpose.text: Give the owner one table that states where the work is, in the simplest form, so a decision can be made without reading prose.
purpose.quote: It has to be simple to use.

invariants.text: The file is a single heading and a single table. Anything else is rejected by the checker.
invariants.quote: It cannot be daunting or overly complex, or no one will use it.

invariants.text: Columns are exactly: #, Work item, Definition of done, Status, Result. (proposed: our convention)
Status is one of Done, In progress, Open, Blocked, Not started. (proposed: our convention)
Every cell is one statement: no semicolons, no parentheses, no dependency words, at most 12 words, work item at most 5. (proposed: our convention)
A Done row carries a measured result, never a pending one.
invariants.quote: A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion

invariants.text: Dependencies live in docs/skill-manifest.json and the ledger, never in the table. (proposed: our convention)

instructions.action: Run python3 tools/status_check.py before and after every edit of STATUS.md.
instructions.why: Proposed: the checker is the definition; a table that fails it is not the status.

instructions.action: Add a work item as one row: a five-word name, a definition of done that is a verifiable statement, a status from the closed set, and a result that is a number or a plain fact.
instructions.why: Proposed: one idea per cell keeps the table readable at a glance.

instructions.action: Write the definition of done as the state that would make the row Done, not as the work to do.
instructions.why: A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion, so state the observable end.
instructions.quote: A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion

instructions.action: Mark a row Done only when the result was measured; otherwise leave it Open or In progress and put the current number in Result.
When a cell needs a second idea, split the row or move the detail to the run summary. Never widen the table.
instructions.why: Proposed: the table is the decision view, not the record.

instructions.action: Keep row numbers contiguous; retire a row by marking it Done or by deleting it and renumbering.
instructions.why: Proposed: stable numbering lets a conversation refer to a row.

best_practices.text: Prefer a number in Result over a word; 29 of 29 beats passing. (proposed: our convention)
Blocked names what blocks it in the Result cell in three words or fewer. (proposed: our convention)
State facts, never reasons, in the table; reasons go to the ceremony records.
best_practices.quote: Products belong in the adapter column only

definition_of_done.breakage: Change one Result cell to a run-on with a dependency word: 'Verified; depends on the loop (see row 5)'

definition_of_done.quote: A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion
